grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.rule: ひと：ひとり、ふたり、さんにん、よにん。かみ：いちまい、にまい、さんまい、よんまい。

tables.caption: The exact hundred and thousand forms shown here
The two different objects in this plan

grammar.note_en:
The estimates and purchases use these numbers:いち one,に two,さん three,よん four,ひゃく one hundred and せん one thousand. The old location particle に does not teach the number two; the old name suffix さん does not teach three. Earlier calendar readings for the 12 th and 13 th are whole date expressions, not a licence to invent other prices. No 5/6/7/8/9 series, tens series or unlimited number generator is assumed here.

A number combines with the kind of thing counted.まい counts flat objects such as these sheets and invitation cards. The whole taught forms are いちまい one sheet,にまい two,さんまい three and よんまい four. In しょうたいじょうがにまいあります,“there are two invitation cards,” the count follows the named object.よんまいのしょうたいじょう means“four invitation cards,” using the already familiar の to connect the count to the noun. Compare the older generic object counter:ふうとうはひとつです,“there is one envelope.” Flat-sheet and generic counts describe things, not people.

The person counter has irregular whole forms:ひとり one person,ふたり two people,さんにん three people and よにん four people. Do not write いちにん,ににん or よんにん. Here ひとり counts one person; in the scene it naturally conveys that Mei stays by herself while the other two leave. In めいはひとり、へやにいます,“Mei stays in the room by herself,” the narrative separates her from the pair going to the shop.ふたりでねだんをききます means“the two of them ask about the price”; the group of two acts together. Money-amount ではたりません means that this amount is insufficient for the named plan; it is a bounded budget construction, not the earlier place で.よにんのなまえ means“the names of four people,” not four names counted as four people.

えん is yen.いくらですか asks a price:“How much is it?” The whole amounts actually shown include ひゃくえん100 yen,にひゃくえん200,さんびゃくえん300,よんひゃくえん400,せんえん1000,にせんえん2000,さんぜんえん3000 and よんせんえん4000. Notice the sound changes in さんびゃく and さんぜん. Do not substitute さんひゃく or さんせん. Use the complete forms shown here; other amounts will come later. A closed price answer is the fixed number phrase plus its currency counter, not a calculation requiring an untaught amount.

よんまいでよんひゃくえんです means“four sheets cost 400 yen.”The count gives the priced quantity;で links that quantity to its total price.ぜんぶでさんぜんえんです means“3000 yen in total.”Compare the known action-location で in みせでなおします,“repair it at the shop”: the same written particle has different constructions.たかい means expensive and やすい means cheap. The story contrasts named figures without introducing the later より comparative.すこし means a little or slightly: it can describe a small amount or modify やすい.

The estimate scopes matter. A new replacement lock costs 4000 yen, beyond the 3000 yen fund. Yesterday's shop-repair estimate is 3000 yen. Repair parts are 2000 yen, but hired tools add 1000 yen, using the same whole fund. That leaves no allocation for invitations. These are fictional shop estimates, not a diagnosis of the cupboard or a claim that any part is guaranteed to fit. No repair or cupboard opening occurs in this chapter.

Haru lends her own tools and says おかねはうけとりません,“I will not take money.” Her tools are not a gift, and she does not donate cash. The removed tool-hire cost makes four small 100 yen invitation copies affordable alongside the 2000 yen parts. The final unspent balance is described only as すこし; no untaught remainder is named. Ren pays the shop, receives the parts and cards, returns, and gives the cards to Mei. He promises to return Haru's tools tomorrow evening.

The two original small invitations were for the 13 thgathering attended by Mei/Ren/Yui and other neighbours at 3:30 p.m.; that meeting happened. Those originals stay in their packet. The new copies concern the later public town reading event tomorrow evening. Four named volunteers receive copies; the public entrance notice also addresses other town readers, so four printed copies are not an attendance limit. This is separate from the later historical-map exhibition. All new number/price words remain kana; the seven new characters here only spell earlier-known calendar/time words, with authored readings on every story occurrence.

notes: Original modern Japanese narrative in four developed scenes. Full40workbook+8A+8B+6Cresponses; no audio or outside-source quotation.
Six cardinal meanings are six separate new units. Only1–4,100and1000and the expressly shown whole counter/price forms are introduced; no hidden unlimited series. New numerical words remain kana.

Seven new script characters spell only earlier-known date/time words. Longest complete declared forms protectあした/いました/ひとつ/ひとりfrom substring corruption. Every emitted Han word receives exact-source authored reading metadata.

The 13th gathering at 3:30 p.m. is retrospectively established as completed, with Mei/Ren/Yui among town neighbours. The new four volunteer copies concern the later formal reading programme on the 16th evening. Neither the original appointment nor the later historical-map exhibition is moved.

Haru is the existing female retired sign painter, distinct from the unnamed female shopowner. She lends her tools without taking money. No lock fault, repair success, parcel contents, map author or unknown receipt signature is established.
Card examples are deliberately selected to make their first matching source occurrence the taught sense. Numericに/さんandじょうrequire special checking against old particles/name suffixes/しょうたいじょう.

Final measurement: 2818 Japanese atoms against plan2840 [2414,3266]; prior coverage76.2% against unchanged part-2 threshold88%. Its actual enumeration finds74 complete count/price expressions,23 in the first third; raw overlapping atom matches are not contextual word counts.
